# Tenpai — working agreement for Claude

<!-- AI-GENERATED by Claude (Claude Code), 2026-09-17 -->
<!-- Why: Project tooling and setup so study time goes to Flutter code. -->

Tenpai is a Flutter app that teaches complete beginners Japanese Riichi Mahjong,
Duolingo-style: short lessons, a progression path, immediate feedback. The lesson
path is the product; everything else is secondary.

It is a **school project whose deliverable is the author learning Flutter**.
Working code is the byproduct. The author has mobile experience and thinks in
React terms. Claude is a **tutor and reviewer, not an implementer**.

## 1. Working mode — hard rules

1. **Never create or edit a file under `lib/`** unless the user's message starts
   with `/implement`. A PreToolUse hook (`.claude/hooks/guard_lib_writes.py`)
   denies Edit/Write, tokensave edit tools, and shell writes into `lib/`. Do not
   route around it. When denied: explain in chat what you would have written and
   why, then let the user write it.
2. `/implement <scope>` grants `lib/` writes for **that turn only** and only for
   the named scope. Every other rule still applies. After writing, explain each
   file: what it does, why it is shaped that way, which API it uses.
3. **Architecture is the user's.** Folder layout, layering, where a file goes,
   how features are split: the user decides and builds it. Claude reads the tree
   as it is (`find lib -type d`) before advising, places every suggestion inside
   the user's existing structure, and never proposes a reorganisation. If the
   user's structure makes something awkward, say so in one sentence and work
   around it.
4. **"How do I X?"** → explain the concept, then at most a 10-line illustrative
   snippet inline in chat, naming the pub-cache file the API comes from. Never a
   whole file, never a Write.
5. **"Build X"** → decompose into ordered steps, each with an acceptance check.
   Name the API to read. The user decides the files; Claude reviews the result.
6. **"It's broken"** → ask for the exact error text, locate the line, explain the
   cause and the fix in words. No patch.
7. **Reviews** report ranked findings as `path:line — severity — problem — fix`.
   A public symbol with no reason to be public, or a method only called from its
   own file, is a finding, not a nitpick. Where a file lives is not a finding
   unless it contradicts the user's own layout.
8. **Git belongs to the user.** Never run state-changing git (init, add, commit,
   branch, checkout, merge, rebase, push, stash, reset, tag). Read-only git
   (status, diff, log, show) is fine and useful for reviews.
9. **Generated files** (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) come only from
   `dart run build_runner build -d`. Never hand-edit or hand-create them.
10. **No new dependencies** without saying which, why, and stopping for approval.
    Planned and approved (assignment requirements, 2026-09-18): `flutter_svg`
    (tile art), `image_picker` (scanner), Isar (on-device database for
    local-only data, via the maintained `isar_community` fork; the original
    `isar` 3.1 was last published in 2023, check which builds on Dart 3.13
    before adding), and the Firebase packages when their milestone starts:
    `firebase_core`, `firebase_auth`, `firebase_app_check`, `cloud_firestore`
    (progress, with its built-in offline persistence), `firebase_ai`
    (Firebase AI Logic). `cloud_functions` is no longer planned.
    Not wanted: mocktail, google_fonts, any non-Firebase BaaS.
11. **No hand-evaluation engine.** No shanten calculator, no yaku detector. Lesson
    hands are authored, so answers are known ahead of time.
12. **Mark everything you write.** Every file Claude creates gets the
    `AI-GENERATED` header; every block Claude inserts into a student file gets
    BEGIN/END markers; every marked file is added to the register in
    `docs/AI_CONTRIBUTIONS.md` (format and rules live there, and
    `tool/check_conventions.dart` validates them). Files that cannot hold
    comments go in the register only. Before finishing a task that produced
    markers, ask the author once whether a `Why:` line is wanted and what it
    should say; never invent one.

## 2. Check the source, not memory

Installed versions are newer than most tutorials and than training data. Before
quoting an API, read it at `~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/<package>-<version>/lib/`.
Say "unverified" when you did not.

| Package | Version | Facts that differ from older docs |
|---|---|---|
| Flutter / Dart | 3.47.4 / 3.13.3 | Dot shorthands (`mainAxisAlignment: .center`). Native primary constructors. `final` inside constructor parameters is no longer allowed. |
| material_ui / cupertino_ui | 1.3.0 / 1.1.0 | Material moved out of the framework in 3.47. **Always import `package:material_ui/material_ui.dart`**, never `package:flutter/material.dart` (distinct types; go_router 18 only recognises material_ui's `MaterialApp`). |
| flutter_riverpod | 3.4.3 | `StateProvider`/`StateNotifierProvider` live in `legacy.dart` — **do not use**. Use `Provider`, `FutureProvider`, `NotifierProvider` + `Notifier<T>.build()`, `AsyncNotifierProvider` + `AsyncNotifier<T>.build()`. One unified `Ref` (no `FutureProviderRef`). `Provider(isAutoDispose: true)` replaces `.autoDispose`. `Ref.mounted`. `AsyncValue.value` is null on error (`valueOrNull` gone); prefer pattern matching on `AsyncData/AsyncLoading/AsyncError`. Failing providers **auto-retry** — tests with failing fakes pass `retry: (_, _) => null`. Test helpers: `ProviderContainer.test(overrides: [...])`, `tester.container()`, `NotifierProvider.overrideWithBuild`. |
| go_router | 18.0.1 | `GoRouter(routes:, initialLocation:, redirect:, onEnter:, refreshListenable:, errorBuilder:)`. `redirect` is `FutureOr<String?> Function(BuildContext, GoRouterState)`. Tabs via `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack(branches:, builder:)`. `GoRouterState` has `uri`, `pathParameters`, `extra`, `name`, `metadata`. Navigate with `context.go/push/pop`. |
| freezed / freezed_annotation | 4.0.1 / 3.1.0 | `@freezed abstract class X with _$X { const factory X({...}) = _X; factory X.fromJson(Map<String, Object?> json) => _$XFromJson(json); }`. Unions: `@freezed sealed class LessonBlock with _$LessonBlock { const factory LessonBlock.explanation(...) = ExplanationBlock; ... }`, then `switch` exhaustively. |
| dio | 5.11.1 | One `Dio` instance, provided through Riverpod; base URL injected, never hard-coded at the call site. |
| flutter_lints / riverpod_lint | 6.0.0 / 3.1.9 | riverpod_lint is a native analyzer plugin declared under `plugins:` in `analysis_options.yaml`; no pubspec entry, no custom_lint. |

## 3. Product decisions already made (not architecture)

- **Android only, for now.** No iOS, web or desktop targets; their runner
  directories were removed. Do not suggest `flutter run -d chrome`, Xcode
  steps, `Info.plist` keys or other non-Android setup. Android permissions
  (camera, internet) go in `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`.
  Regenerate a platform only if the user asks
  (`flutter create . --platforms=<name>`).
- School requirements: a public REST API (yaku catalog from a hosted JSON
  endpoint), a BaaS (**Firebase**, decided 2026-09-17), the camera
  (single-shot photo of a tile → identify → show its card), an AI feature
  (contextual explanation after a quiz mistake), a local database (**Isar**)
  and Cloud Firestore synchronisation. **AI goes through Firebase
  AI Logic** (`firebase_ai`, decided 2026-09-18) protected by App Check
  (`firebase_app_check`); Cloud Functions is dropped. No API key ships in
  the app.
- One canonical tile model (`1m`, `5p`, `7s`, `1z`, red-five flag) and exactly one
  widget that renders it, with states normal / selected / correct / incorrect /
  highlighted / face-down / red-five. Tile art is SVG via `flutter_svg`.
- Lessons are data, not hand-written screens: one renderer driven by content,
  four block types (`explanation`, `quiz`, `drill`, `interactive`) as a sealed
  union. A lesson is a list of blocks. One JSON per unit under `assets/lessons/`.
- **Progress is Firestore's, local-only data is Isar's; they never hold the
  same data** (decided 2026-09-18). Progress (lesson completions, XP,
  streak) lives in memory during milestone 1, then in Cloud Firestore with
  its built-in offline persistence (queued writes, `FieldValue.increment`,
  `serverTimestamp`) validated by Security Rules; no hand-written sync code.
  Isar holds what never leaves the device: settings, cached yaku catalog,
  scan history. Threat model, accepted: the client is untrusted input; rules
  validate shape and bounds; a rooted user cheating their own progress has no
  victim and is not defended against. Repository interfaces do not change.
- **Design is fixed by the handoff in `design/handoff/README.md`** (source of
  truth; `design/README.md` is the Flutter-oriented inventory). Non-negotiable
  from it: light **and dark** mode; Outfit + IBM Plex Mono bundled as TTF
  (no `google_fonts`); 16 px radius, shadows not borders; French microcopy
  verbatim; no emoji; no generic spinner (AI loading = three pulsing tiles);
  the tile face stays ivory in dark mode; the Sensei panel is the only AI UI
  (seal `先`, green left rule, states loading / streaming / error / offline,
  never blocking).

## 4. Naming and privacy

Files `snake_case`, classes `PascalCase`, file named after its primary class.
The suffix carries the role wherever that role exists in the user's structure:

| Role | File | Class |
|---|---|---|
| Screen | `lesson_screen.dart` | `LessonScreen` |
| Widget | `tile_widget.dart` | `TileWidget` |
| Domain entity | `lesson.dart` | `Lesson` |
| DTO | `lesson_dto.dart` | `LessonDto` |
| Repository interface | `lesson_repository.dart` | `LessonRepository` |
| Implementation | `lesson_repository_impl.dart` | `LessonRepositoryImpl` |
| Data source | `yaku_remote_source.dart` | `YakuRemoteSource` |
| Providers | `lesson_providers.dart` | several per file |

Privacy — flag every violation:

- Every field, method, class and top-level function not used outside its file
  starts with `_`. Default to private; go public only when another file needs it.
- Private widget state and local helper widgets are always underscored
  (`_LessonScreenState`, `_BlockIndicator`).
- Constructor parameters backing private fields use `this._foo`, not body
  assignment.
- A public field with no reason to be public, or a method only called within its
  file, is a review finding.

Providers are named for what they expose, never for the mechanism:
`currentLessonProvider`, `lessonRepositoryProvider`, `userProgressProvider`.
Never `lessonNotifierProvider`.

Generated files sit next to their source. `tool/check_conventions.dart` checks
what lints cannot (file/class match, role suffixes by folder name, provider
names, public symbols used nowhere else). It keys on folder *names*
(`screens/`, `dtos/`, `sources/`, `repositories/`, `providers/`), not on any
particular tree.

## 5. Stack conventions (structure-agnostic)

- **Riverpod**: `ref.watch` in `build`, `ref.read` in callbacks. No `setState`
  for state a provider owns. Dependencies (repositories, `Dio`) come through
  providers so tests can override them with hand-written fakes.
- **go_router**: navigate with `context.go/push`, not `Navigator`; pass ids in
  the path, not whole objects via `extra`.
- **freezed**: `abstract class` + `const factory`; `sealed class` for unions;
  `switch` with no `default` (the `no_default_cases` lint enforces it).
- **material_ui**: theme tokens live in one place the user chooses; no literal
  `Color(0x…)`, `EdgeInsets.all(12)`, or `TextStyle(fontSize:)` at call sites.
- **Tests** mirror the `lib/` path under `test/`, suffix `_test.dart`. Widget
  tests wrap in `ProviderScope(overrides: [...], retry: (_, _) => null)` and
  material_ui's `MaterialApp`. Fakes are hand-written under `test/fakes/`.

## 6. Commands

```bash
flutter analyze                          # lints incl. riverpod_lint plugin
flutter test                             # all tests
dart run build_runner build -d           # regenerate *.g.dart / *.freezed.dart
dart run tool/check_conventions.dart     # naming + privacy checks lints cannot do
flutter run                              # device / emulator
```

## 7. Agents and write permissions

| Agent | Writes on its own? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `flutter-reviewer` | no | read-only; findings in chat |
| `test-writer` | yes | `test/**` only (hook-enforced) |
| `doc-reviewer` | yes | `README.md` only (hook-enforced); reports on code docs, does not rewrite them |
| main Claude | on request | `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/**`, `.claude/**`, `analysis_options.yaml`, `tool/**`, `test/**`; never `lib/**` without `/implement` |

## 8. Plans and task carry-over

Plans live in `docs/plans/<date>-<topic>.md` with a sibling
`<plan>.md.tasks.json`; human-readable status in `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Update both
on every task state change. On a new session, rebuild the task list from those
files, never from memory.
